message.content:
**Famous Dancers of the 19th Century**

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions / Roles |
|------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swedish-Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1879) | Austrian | Renowned for her virtuosity and dramatic flair; performed across Europe and the U.S. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Master choreographer; created many ballets that remain classics (e.g., *The Sleeping Beauty*, *Swan Lake*). |
| **Jean Coralli** (1797–1865) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle* (1841); known for his elegant style. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1810–1880) | Italian | Influential ballet teacher; authored *L’Art de la Danse* (1853). |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though born in the late 19th century, she rose to fame in the early 20th; her legacy began in the 19th‑century ballet tradition. |
| **John L. T. (John L. T.)** | American | Early American ballet pioneer; performed in the U.S. and Europe. |
| **Giovanni Battista Viotti** (1766–1824) | Italian | Though primarily a violinist, he was also a celebrated dancer in his youth. |
| **Eugène Scribe** (1791–1861) | French | Playwright and librettist who collaborated with choreographers on many 19th‑century productions. |
| **Félix de Mérode** (1815–1890) | Belgian | Noted for his expressive dance style in operatic productions. |

> **Note:** The 19th century was a transformative period for ballet and dance, with many performers pushing the boundaries of technique and expression. The above list highlights some of the most influential figures whose work shaped the art form during that era.
